findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted
findings.body: In isAccessTokenId(), the condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the shortcut MATCHES the expected value, and implicitly returns true (falls through to isUUID check) when it does NOT match. This is backwards: the matcher should fail (return false) when the shortcut does not equal the expected grant shortcut, and succeed when it does. As written, tests using this matcher will pass when the grant type encoding is wrong and fail when it's correct, defeating the purpose of the assertion and potentially masking real encoding bugs.

findings.title: Refresh grant type hardcoded instead of using actual context grant type
findings.body: In validateToken (used when refreshing tokens), `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN)` unconditionally sets the grant type to refresh_token. However this method can be invoked in different token-refresh contexts (e.g., token-exchange or other flows reusing validateToken), so hardcoding REFRESH_TOKEN may encode an incorrect grant-type shortcut into the new access token ID, misleading consumers who rely on the encoded context for optimization decisions.

findings.title: Lazy-refresh of grant maps has race/DoS potential and no synchronization
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut fall back to scanning all OAuth2GrantType factories and mutating the shared ConcurrentHashMap when a grant type/shortcut is unknown. If an attacker repeatedly sends access tokens with bogus/invalid grant shortcuts, each lookup triggers a full stream scan of all grant type factories (via sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream) on every call without caching the negative result, which can be used for a minor CPU-amplification/DoS vector, and there's no synchronization protecting concurrent writes to the two maps, which could leave them transiently inconsistent under concurrent access.

findings.title: Wrong variable null-checked in constructor
findings.body: In the AccessTokenContext constructor, the null check `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. As a result, passing a null rawTokenId will not throw the intended NPE with a correct message, and a null rawTokenId can slip through into token ID encoding, producing a malformed token ID (e.g., 'xxxxx:null').
